questions.q: State what the Domain Name Service does.

markPoints.concept: it translates a domain name into an IP address
markPoints.exemplar: It translates a domain name into an IP address.

questions.example: It translates a domain name such as revise360.co.uk into the IP address of the server that holds the site.
questions.paraphrase: It converts a web address people type into the numerical address computers use.
questions.feedback: Name in, address out. Both halves are needed.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.3 Lesson 5 — Inside the internet, station 2: Domain Name Service (DNS)

questions.q: Put these steps in order for what happens when a user types a web address into a browser.
steps: The browser asks a domain name server for the IP address
The domain name server returns the IP address
The browser requests the page from the web server at that address
The web server sends the page back to the browser
questions.feedback: The name has to become an address before anything can be requested.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.3 Lesson 5 — Inside the internet, station 2: Domain Name Service (DNS)

questions.q: A domain name server does not have the address being asked for. What happens?
options: It passes the request on to another domain name server
The page cannot be loaded and an error is shown immediately
The browser guesses the IP address from the domain name
The request is sent to every computer on the internet
questions.feedback: DNS is a hierarchy: a server that does not know asks one that is more likely to.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.3 Lesson 5 — Inside the internet, station 2: Domain Name Service (DNS)

questions.q: Explain what is meant by 'the cloud'.

markPoints.concept: data and software are stored on remote servers rather than on the user's own device
markPoints.exemplar: Data is stored on remote servers rather than on the user's own computer.

markPoints.concept: and is reached over the internet from any device
markPoints.exemplar: It is reached over the internet from any device.

questions.example: The cloud means storing data and running software on remote servers owned by someone else, rather than on your own computer, and reaching them over the internet from any device.
questions.paraphrase: Your files and programs live on somebody else's machines in a data centre, and you get at them through the internet from wherever you are.
questions.feedback: Somewhere else, reached over the internet. 'The cloud is the internet' is not enough on its own.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.3 Lesson 5 — Inside the internet, station 2: Domain Name Service (DNS)
